data.heading: Introduction to Modern Web Development
data.subtitle: From Zero to Hero — Interactive Workshop
data.speakerNotes: Welcome everyone! Today we'll explore the fundamentals of modern web development. This workshop is designed for complete beginners. Let's make this interactive and fun!

data.heading: Learning Objectives

items.text: Understand HTML structure and semantic elements
items.detail: HTML is the skeleton of every webpage. Semantic elements like <header>, <nav>, <main>, and <footer> give meaning to your content.

items.text: Master CSS styling and modern layout techniques
items.detail: CSS controls visual presentation. Flexbox and Grid are the two modern layout systems every developer needs to know.

items.text: Write interactive JavaScript for dynamic behavior
items.detail: JavaScript brings pages to life with event handling, DOM manipulation, and asynchronous operations.

items.text: Build responsive designs for all devices
items.detail: Media queries and fluid layouts ensure your website looks great on phones, tablets, and desktops.

items.text: Deploy your first project to the web
items.detail: Services like Netlify, Vercel, and GitHub Pages make deployment free and instant.

data.speakerNotes: Walk through each objective. Click each bullet to reveal the detailed explanation. Ask the audience which topic they're most excited about.

data.heading: The Web Technology Stack

items.title: HTML — The Structure
items.content: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) defines the structure and content of web pages. Think of it as the blueprint of a building — it determines what rooms exist and where they are, but not how they look.

items.title: CSS — The Style
items.content: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the visual presentation. Colors, fonts, spacing, animations — everything visual is CSS. Modern CSS includes powerful features like Grid, Custom Properties, and Container Queries.

items.title: JavaScript — The Behavior
items.content: JavaScript makes pages interactive and dynamic. From simple button clicks to complex single-page applications, JS is the programming language of the web. Modern JS (ES2024+) is powerful and expressive.

items.title: DevTools — Your Best Friend
items.content: Every modern browser includes Developer Tools (F12). The Elements panel lets you inspect HTML/CSS live. The Console lets you run JavaScript. The Network panel shows all HTTP requests. Master these tools early!

data.speakerNotes: Open each accordion section one by one. For the code examples, consider showing a live demo in VS Code. Ask students: 'Which layer do you think is the hardest to learn?'

data.heading: CSS Layout Methods Compared

tabs.label: Flexbox
tabs.content: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout method for arranging items in rows OR columns. It excels at distributing space and aligning items within a container. Perfect for navigation bars, card rows, and centering content.

tabs.label: CSS Grid
tabs.content: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system for rows AND columns simultaneously. It's ideal for page-level layouts, complex dashboards, and any design requiring precise placement in both dimensions.

tabs.label: Container Queries
tabs.content: Container Queries let components adapt based on their parent container's size, not the viewport. This is a game-changer for reusable components that need to work in different contexts.
features: Based on parent size, not viewport

data.speakerNotes: Switch between tabs to compare the three layout methods. Emphasize that Flexbox and Grid are complementary, not competing. Container Queries are the newest and most exciting addition.

data.heading: Building Your First Webpage

steps.title: Step 1: Create the HTML file
steps.content: Create a new file called index.html. Add the basic HTML5 boilerplate with <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head>, and <body> tags. This is the foundation of every web page.
steps.tip: Use the '!' shortcut in VS Code to generate boilerplate instantly.

steps.title: Step 2: Add your content
steps.content: Inside the <body> tag, add semantic HTML elements: a <header> with your site title, a <main> section with an <article> containing your content, and a <footer> with copyright info.
steps.tip: Always use semantic elements instead of generic <div> tags — it improves accessibility and SEO.

steps.title: Step 3: Style with CSS
steps.content: Create a styles.css file and link it in your <head>. Start with a CSS reset, then add your custom styles using modern features like custom properties, flexbox, and gradients.
steps.tip: Set box-sizing: border-box on everything first — it makes sizing much more intuitive.

steps.title: Step 4: Add interactivity
steps.content: Create a script.js file and link it before the closing </body> tag. Add event listeners for user interactions like clicks, hover effects, and form submissions.
steps.tip: Use 'defer' attribute on your <script> tag so it doesn't block page rendering.

steps.title: Step 5: Deploy to the web
steps.content: Push your code to GitHub, then connect the repository to Netlify or Vercel for instant, free deployment. Every push to main will automatically update your live site.
steps.tip: Add a custom domain later — most registrars offer .dev domains for around $12/year.

data.speakerNotes: Walk through each step one at a time. At each step, show the corresponding code on screen. Give students 2 minutes per step to follow along on their own laptops.

data.heading: Key Concepts — Flip to Learn

cards.back: Document Object Model — the tree-like representation of your HTML that JavaScript can read and modify in real time.
Application Programming Interface — a contract that allows two software systems to communicate. REST and GraphQL are the most common web API patterns.
Single Page Application — a web app that loads once and dynamically updates content without full page reloads. React, Vue, and Angular build SPAs.
Server-Side Rendering — HTML is generated on the server for each request. Improves SEO and initial load time. Next.js and Nuxt.js support SSR.
Progressive Web App — a website that can be installed like a native app, works offline, and sends push notifications. Uses Service Workers and Web Manifests.
Accessibility — designing websites usable by everyone, including people with disabilities. Use semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and keyboard navigation.

data.speakerNotes: Have students click each card to flip it. After revealing all definitions, ask them to close their eyes and quiz them: 'What does SPA stand for?'

data.heading: Quick Check — Test Your Knowledge

questions.question: Which language is used to define the STRUCTURE of a web page?
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) defines the structure and content of web pages. CSS handles styling, and JavaScript handles behavior.

questions.question: What CSS property creates a two-dimensional layout?
questions.explanation: CSS Grid (display: grid) is the two-dimensional layout system. Flexbox is one-dimensional (row OR column).

questions.question: What does 'responsive design' mean?
questions.explanation: Responsive design means the layout adapts to different viewport sizes — from mobile phones to wide desktop monitors — using media queries and fluid layouts.

data.speakerNotes: Run through the quiz interactively. Have students vote by raising hands before revealing answers. Celebrate correct answers!

data.heading: React vs. Vue — Framework Comparison
data.verdict: Both are excellent choices. React offers more flexibility and job opportunities. Vue offers a smoother learning experience and better documentation.
data.speakerNotes: Present this as a friendly comparison, not a competition. Emphasize that the best framework is the one you enjoy using. Ask students which they'd like to try first.

data.heading: Web Development Evolution

events.title: The First Website
events.description: Tim Berners-Lee publishes the first-ever website at CERN. It was a simple text page explaining the World Wide Web project.

events.title: CSS Is Born
events.description: CSS1 is released, finally separating content (HTML) from presentation (CSS). Web design becomes a real discipline.

events.title: jQuery Revolution
events.description: jQuery simplifies DOM manipulation and AJAX. 'Write less, do more' becomes the mantra. It dominated for a decade.

events.title: React Changes Everything
events.description: Facebook releases React with its virtual DOM and component model. The era of modern SPA frameworks begins.

events.title: Jamstack & Edge
events.description: Static site generators, serverless functions, and edge computing reshape how we build and deploy web applications.

events.title: AI-Powered Development
events.description: AI coding assistants, automated testing, and intelligent design tools transform the developer experience.

data.speakerNotes: Scroll through the timeline slowly. At each milestone, share a fun fact or personal anecdote about that era. Ask senior developers in the audience to share their experiences.

data.heading: Key Takeaways
items: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript form the core web technology stack
Modern layout uses Flexbox (1D) and Grid (2D)
Semantic HTML improves accessibility and SEO
Start simple, deploy early, iterate often
The web platform is more powerful than ever
data.callToAction: Start building today — your first website is just 3 files away!
data.speakerNotes: Recap the key points. Encourage students to start a personal project this week. Share the resource links. Open the floor for Q&A.
